sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: This example is written more briefly. Fill in the reasoning it leaves out.

items.prompt: A meal has 3 main dish options and 2 side options. How many different meals are possible?

steps: Identify the favorable outcomes and the total possible outcomes.
Write the probability as a reduced fraction, or use it to predict or evaluate a count.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Work these with your teaching parent. Say the reason for each step out loud before you write it.

items.prompt: A probability model predicts a fair 4-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 30 times in 120 spins. A simulation of 120 spins landed on that section 31 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 0. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
A spinner was spun 60 times and landed on blue 20 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A bag has 2 red, 4 blue, and 10 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
A fair coin is flipped and a spinner with 5 equal sections numbered 1 to 5 is spun. What is the probability of getting heads on the coin and landing on 3 on the spinner?
A outfit is made by choosing one shirt color from 3 options and one shorts color from 4 options. How many different outfits are possible?

A probability model predicts a fair 5-section spinner lands on a chosen section about 34 times in 170 spins. A simulation of 170 spins landed on that section 29 times. How does the simulated count compare to the model's prediction?
An event has a probability of 1/10. How would you describe how likely the event is to happen?
choices: equally likely to happen or not happen

sections.title: Mastery check
sections.directions: Mastery check. Work without help, then stop and hand this section in.

items.prompt: A spinner was spun 50 times and landed on blue 23 times. Based on this experiment, what is the experimental probability of landing on blue?
A bag has 4 red, 5 blue, and 12 green marbles. If one marble is drawn at random, what is the theoretical probability of drawing red, P(red)?
